verdict.rationale: Aider's docs say it lints the files it edits by default, and it can run tests via /test or automatically with --test-cmd/--auto-test. It also accepts requests for test cases, so test writing and lint/test feedback loops are supported. Nothing in the evidence covers resolving merge conflicts or updating dependencies, and the docs only say it lints edited files, not that it fixes the errors it finds. Missing for 10: documented merge-conflict resolution, documented dependency updating, explicit evidence that lint errors are fixed automatically, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent write tests, fix lint errors, resolve merge conflicts, and update dependencies for me

citations.quote: By default, aider will lint any files which it edits.
You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
Request new features, test cases or bug fixes using your voice and let aider do the work of editing the files in your local git repo.
